Our Why

Why AfroBot exists

AfroBot is a platform for the African dream. We’re opening up practical AI and robotics education for young people in Africa and other communities where access is limited.

Get involvedExplore AfroBot

The platform

Students learn at their own pace, build and test their ideas, and use what they learn to tackle problems they know firsthand. We invite Africans and friends of Africa to help give more young people the tools, mentorship, and opportunities to build solutions for their communities.

Why access matters

A chance to build should not depend on a school’s budget

A young person’s chance to learn AI and robotics should never depend on where they’re born or what their school can afford. When students get to build something themselves, they learn to ask better questions, test an idea, and improve it when it fails. We want more young people to have that experience and turn those skills into opportunities for themselves and their communities.

Vision and mission

What we are here to do

Vision. Young people across Africa have the skills and opportunity to shape their communities’ future through AI and robotics.

Mission. Make hands-on AI and robotics education accessible to young people with limited access, equip local coaches to teach it, and help students turn what they learn into solutions for their communities.

How students take part

Learn, build, get support, and share

  1. 1

    Learn

    Self-paced Moodle lessons are planned for students and instructors, with activities designed for schools with limited equipment.

  2. 2

    Build

    In AfroBot Workbench, students will practice with hands-on exercises like training an image model for a tabletop sorter, then apply what they learn to problems they choose. That sorter is an illustrative practice example, not a story of a particular student.

  3. 3

    Get support

    Local coaches help students test ideas, learn from mistakes, and improve their projects.

  4. 4

    Share

    The AfroBot competition will give students a place to demonstrate what they built, explain whom it helps, and show what changed after testing.

Where this builds from

A newer initiative

This work builds on more than three years of student learning in Bamenda through Glappy Foundation, operating there as Glappy Village. AfroBot is the newer initiative that builds on that experience and brings young people together through robotics and AI.
